NOTES 
{l) Contracting 
for 
Specific 
Performance. 
Orders 
of specific 
performance are commonly based on the equitable desertion exercised by 
courts when money damages are deemed inadequate 
or when specific 
performance is the conventional remedy for breach, such cases involving a 
sale of real property. However, courts may grant specific performance not 
only for their own discretionary or conventional reasons, but also when the 
parties' agreement expresses a clear intention for specific performance. On 
what basis was the specific performance 
order reasoned in Snow Phipps'? 
Grants of specific performance in the merger context was not unfamiliar in 
Delaware, but after Vice Chancellor Strine's opinion In re IBP, Inc. S'holders 
Litig., 789 A.2d 14, 82 (Del. Ch. 2001), wherein 
he ordered specific 
performance while applying New York law, sophisticated contracting parti s 
have tended to stipulate specific performance in their merger agreements. 
See John C. Coates, Managing Disputes 
through Contract: Evidence from 
M&A, 2 Harv. Bus. L. Rev. 295 (2012); Theresa Arnold, Amanda Dixon, 
Hadar Tanne, Madison Whalen Sherrill & Mitu Gulati, "Lipstick on a Pig": 
Specific Performance Clauses in Action, 2021 Wis. L. Rev. 359. 
(2) Having KCAKE and Damages Too. Note how quickly an order of 
specific performance may be effectuated 
for in merger context. It was not 
unreasonable for the plaintiffs in Snow Phipps to ask the Court to order 
Kohlberg "to close within fifteen days of [its] decision." Timing is often of the 
essence in high-stakes 
merger and acquisition disputes, 
and Delawar 
Chancery has a reputation of resolving these matters expeditiously once they 
are presented before the Court, as illustrated in the letter below involving a 
recent merger dispute that reached wide public consciousness: 
Defendants [Elon R. Musk, X Holdings I, Inc., and X Holdings II, 
Inc.] have stated that "the closing is expected on or around October 
28, 2022." Plaintiff Twitter, Inc. opposes the motion on the basis 
that Defendants' agreement will not ensure that the transaction 
closes fast enough. 
This action is stayed until 
5 p.m. on October 28, 2022, to 
permit the parties to close on the transaction. If the transaction
